1.sofaString: 104	Pt, '*****', is a 4 month old male[FP1] who is diagnosed with progressive heart failure, Noonans disorder, ASK, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, s/p pacemaker who is being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment[FP2].  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's mother and review of the medical records.   SW spent 75 minutes of face to face time with patient and family.     Living situation:  Pt, *****, lives with his parents and siblings[FP3] in **** **** *****, *******.  They reside in a duplex[FP4].  They live in * **** with city water and central heating and a/c[FP5].  There is no smoking in the home[FP6].  They have no pets[FP7].       Demographics:  Mother: ****** ********  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  33  Education:  Some college[FP8]  Employment:  Not employed[FP9]  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ***** ********  DOB:  **/**/****     Age:  41  Employment:  Works as a property manager[FP10]  ******:  $35,000/ year  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  Sister: ***   ***:  **/**/****   Age:  11  Sister:  *****  DOB **/**/****   Age 8  Brother:  *****    DOB **/**/****    Age 18 months     Support systems:  ****** reports that they receive most of their support from one another[FP11].  She denies any extended family members nearby.  She denies being part of a local ****** community[FP12].  She states it is up to them to take care of the children.  However, she states they are trying to get dad's sister here from *******.  However, she cannot come until **** and is unsure if she can get a visa to travel due to current political climate.  *****, who is from *******,i is not currently a ******* but does have a green card.  He has applied for citizenship.  He has been in the United States since 1999[FP13].  ****** disclosed that they have been married for 12 years[FP14].     ****** initially stated that transportation is not a problem.  She disclosed that they own a 2016 ***** CRV[FP15].  However, she then disclosed that she and ***** share this vehicle, and he currently has the vehicle[FP16]. She is using **** to get around.  She states she will have to **** a car post-transplant in order to get ***** to his appts, as she does not want to use Medicaid[FP17] transportation[FP18]. She states she cannot fathom moving the car seat base from car to car as using Medicaid[FP19] transportation would require.  She does not want to use the car seat without the base.  She also later disclosed that the cost of the gas may be challenging[FP20].  She states she is open to applying for a First Hand Foundation *****.  Fundraising through **** was also discussed.  However, she is unsure if she wants to do this because she does not want photos or information about ***** getting out[FP21].       ****** disclosed she has researched transplant extensively and is aware that they will need to stay in local housing for 2-4 months after transplant[FP22].   SW advised that we typically keep families 4-6 weeks.  She would not receive this and reiterated that she has done her research already[FP23].  ****** asked about transplant housing.  SW explained that this was typically a 2 or 3 bedroom condo, and that the other children would be able to stay here during that time as well if they were out of school.  ****** initially disclosed that she does not want ***** exposed to their germs and would prefer to keep them away[FP24].  However, she later disclosed that after discussing with *****, they realized it might be helpful to be able to have the others here[FP25].  Of note, she had also mentioned building a barrier in their home to keep ***** more isolated from the other children in order to keep him less at risk of infections[FP26].  However, she seems to understand now that is not warranted[FP27].     Course of illness:     ***** is a 4 m.o. male[FP28] with ****** syndrome and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with atrial tachyarrhythmias s/p ablasion and myomectomy. He developed complete AV block after EPS and was placed on pacemaker. Transferred here with worsening respiratory distress and tachyarrhythmias for further management.      Financial Situation:     ***** is covered by Medicaid[FP29] ******.  The family is applying her for SSI/ disability[FP30].  The family is supported by dad's employment income.  ****** was ambivalent in regards to applying for WIC benefits[FP31]. She disclosed that they have more than adequate supply of formula at home already[FP32]. She states they have so much that she is fearful it will expire before he can use it.  ****** is interested in applying for First Hand Foundation[FP33].  She verbalizes understanding that the transplant housing is expensive.  However, she is somewhat ambivalent about fundraising to assist with these expenses[FP34].  Information on fundraising through **** was provided.      Family History:     ****** disclosed a complicated family history for herself and for *****.  She disclosed that there was a history of substance abuse with her parents[FP35], and disclosed growing up in an abusive environment[FP36].  She describes being abandoned by her parents as well[FP37].  She disclosed that her father passed away on **/**/**** of a heart issue. However she does now know the specifics regarding this heart condition.  ****** states her mother had congestive heart failure which was related to her substance abuse[FP38].  ****** disclosed that *****'s father had ***** and passed away when ***** was 11 yrs old.  *****'s mother had a blood clot in her leg and also passed away while ***** was a young child.  ****** denies any medical problems for herself or *****.   *****'s older brother was born with a cleft palate, which has now been surgically corrected.  There is no other reported medical history for the family.      ****** denies a history of mental health issues[FP39] until ***** was born. She now reports that she experienced PTSD[FP40] from the hospital stay in *****.  She also describes a great amount of anxiety[FP41].  She states she has been diagnosed with blepharitis in her right eye that is entirely due to stress[FP42].  She states she was given a prescription for 8 pills of Ativan at an urgent care in *****, and states it does seem helpful.  However, she has been resistant to taking these as she does not have a means of getting refills[FP43].  Her insurance is not accepted at the providers in Gainesville[FP44].  SW advised that she could be seen in the ED.  However, she was initially resistant to this. She disclosed she did not want to leave ***** while being 'stuck' in the ED for hours.  However, she has since decided that she will go there when her husband is here this weekend so that ***** is not alone.  ****** describes herself as experiencing tachycardia due to the anxiety[FP45]. She also describes having difficulty breathing when she is really anxious[FP46].  She has agreed to a psychological evaluation, which has been scheduled[FP47].     ****** denies any other family mental health history.       ****** denies any substance abuse in the immediate family, but does report extensive past substance abuse in her extended family[FP48].  There is no reported history of DV or involvement with DCF[FP49].       Adherence:  ****** has verbalized that she knows more than the nurses and doctors about her child's care.  There are concerns that she may not be compliant with administering meds as prescribed due to belief that she knows best.  She reports that she is the one who managed his meds while in the hospital in *****, telling nurses what meds he needed at what times.  She was observed complaining to a nurse here about the quantity of blood taken for labs.  There are concerns that she may try to interfere with care or attempt to dictate care[FP50].         Assessment and recommendations:     ****** expresses a willingness to move forward with transplant.  She verbalizes belief that ***** has only 2 options:  transplant or death.  However, the plan of care is still being determined and it is possible that he may not need a transplant, but can be managed or with other surgical options.         IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  2     Family Background & Social Support -  3     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 4     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 2     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  1     Coping Skills - 4     Total:  21 Moderate/High Risk     The family scores as moderate/high risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concern is ******'s high anxiety and poor coping skills.  In addition, the lack of support persons is concerning.  In addition, the family has limited finances, resides 4 hours away and are sharing a vehicle.  Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teach-back method to ensure that the family understands what is being explained.  *Provide fundraising and financial resources to assist the family with expenses that arise secondary to child's extended admission   *Assist with connecting ****** with counseling and psychiatric supports that will assist in positive coping skills.  Monitor adherence to these supports[FP51].        ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****[FP1]Gender[FP2]ACC_Health_Care[FP3]Living_Condition[FP4]Living_Condition[FP5]Living_Supply[FP6]Smoking[FP7]Living_Condition[FP8]Education_General[FP9]Employment_Status[FP10]Occupation[FP11]Social_Cohesion[FP12]Social_Support[FP13]Citizenship/Nationality[FP14]Marriage_Status[FP15]Financial_Constraint[FP16]Financial_Constraint[FP17]Insurance[FP18]Financial_Constraint[FP19]Insurance[FP20]Financial_Constraint[FP21]Financial_Constraint[FP22]Living_Condition[FP23]Literacy[FP24]Literacy[FP25]Social_Cohesion[FP26]Literacy[FP27]Literacy[FP28]gender[FP29]Insurance[FP30]Insurance[FP31]Poverty[FP32]Living_Supply[FP33]Financial_Constraint[FP34]Financial_Constraint[FP35]Drug_Abuse (Historical)[FP36]Abuse (Historical)[FP37]Abuse[FP38]Drug_Abuse[FP39]Mental Health[FP40]Mental Health[FP41]Mental Health[FP42]Mental Health[FP43]Mental Health[FP44]Insurance[FP45]Mental Health[FP46]Mental Health[FP47]Mental Health[FP48]Substance_Abuse[FP49]Abuse[FP50]Adherence[FP51]Reccomendations
